# Design: Device identity in multiplayer

## Overview

```
 friend's selecle                         host
   hello { device: { id, publicKey } } ──▶  claim saved, nonce made
                         ◀── prove { nonce }
   proof { signature } ───────────────────▶  verifyDevice → device = id (or null)
   (name, room code typed as before)         deviceReady() → me = { device, uid: "dev:<id>" }
```

The stream is ordered and a selecle client says hello the moment it connects, so when the room code
has been read a hello has either arrived or never will. Plain Telnet is never delayed.

## Components and Interfaces

### `src/device.js`
- `makeDevice()`, `loadDevice(file)` (cached; in-memory under `node --test` without `SELECLE_HOME`),
  `resetDevice()`, `fingerprint(publicKey)`, `publicPart(d)`, `proveDevice(d, nonce)`,
  `verifyDevice({ id, publicKey, nonce, signature })`, `newNonce()`, `shortDevice(id)`, `DEVICE_OK`.

### `src/remote.js`
- Host side: `hello` (once per connection) → `prove`; `proof` → verified `device`;
  `deviceReady(proofMs = 3000)`.
- Client side: hello v2 with `publicPart(device)`; `prove` → `proof`. `agents.device` for tests;
  each pretend friend under test gets its own device.

### `src/telnet.js`
- `keyOf(person)` = `dev:<id>` or `name:<name>`; `mayConjure(person)`, `mayTouch(person)`.
- `bind(name, device)` moves name rules to the device at join; `keyFor(name)` for host commands.
- The identity: `makeIdentity(name, { device, uid: "dev:<id>" })`.

### `src/profile.js`, `src/context.js`, `bin/selecle.js`
- `identityOf` adds `device`; events `by` and presence carry it; `whoami` prints it.

## Data Models

- `~/.selecle/device.json`: `{ id, publicKey (spki DER, base64), privateKey (pkcs8 DER, base64), createdAt }`.
- Host rules: `rules.named: Map<key, boolean>`, `trusted: Set<key>`, key = `dev:<id>` | `name:<name>`.

## Error Handling

| Case | Behaviour |
|---|---|
| Damaged device file | a new device is made |
| Home not writable | the device lives for this run only |
| Hello claims another device's id | its proof fails; the guest has no device |
| Replayed proof | fails: the nonce is new for every connection |
| No proof within 3 s | no device (known by name) |

## Testing Strategy

`test/device.test.js`: keys and proofs (wrong nonce, other key, mismatched id, garbage); the file;
your own identity; the in-memory handshake (valid, spoofed, old client, no hello); a real host and
`selecle join` clients over TCP (uid by device, `who`, trust surviving a rename, a stranger with a
trusted name, name rules binding to the first device, plain Telnet).
